scenes.title: The Princes of Ayodhya
scenes.narration: Long ago, in the golden city of Ayodhya, King Dasharatha ruled a prosperous kingdom with wisdom and love. He was blessed with four sons: Rama, Bharata, Lakshmana, and Shatrughna. Among them, Rama shone brightest — calm, truthful, and compassionate. The great sage Vishwamitra arrived one day, seeking Rama and Lakshmana's help to protect sacred rituals from dark forces. Thus began the journey that would shape the world.

subtitles.text: Long ago, in the golden city of Ayodhya, King Dasharatha ruled a prosperous kingdom with wisdom and love.
He was blessed with four sons: Rama, Bharata, Lakshmana, and Shatrughna.
Among them, Rama shone brightest — calm, truthful, and compassionate.
The great sage Vishwamitra arrived one day, seeking Rama and Lakshmana's help to protect sacred rituals from dark forces.
Thus began the journey that would shape the world.

dialogue.speaker: dasharatha
dialogue.text: My sons, our kingdom thrives, but darkness looms. We must protect our sacred rituals!

dialogue.speaker: rama
dialogue.text: Fear not, Father. Lakshmana and I will stand against any threat to Ayodhya.

dialogue.speaker: lakshmana
dialogue.text: Together, we are unstoppable! Let them come!

dialogue.speaker: vibhishana
dialogue.text: Even the mightiest can falter; choose dharma over power, dear brother.

dialogue.speaker: hanuman
dialogue.text: I shall carry your message to Sita! She must know of your resolve!

scenes.title: Sita and the Bow of Shiva
scenes.narration: In the kingdom of Mithila, King Janaka held a great challenge: whoever could lift and string the mighty bow of Shiva would win the hand of his daughter, Sita. Many powerful kings tried and failed. When Rama stepped forward, he not only lifted the bow but broke it with ease. The assembly watched in awe. Sita placed the garland around Rama's neck. Their union was celebrated across both kingdoms.

subtitles.text: In the kingdom of Mithila, King Janaka held a great challenge: whoever could lift and string the mighty bow of Shiva would win the hand of his daughter, Sita.
Many powerful kings tried and failed.
When Rama stepped forward, he not only lifted the bow but broke it with ease.
The assembly watched in awe.
Sita placed the garland around Rama's neck.
Their union was celebrated across both kingdoms.

dialogue.speaker: sita
dialogue.text: At last, a true hero stands before us! May he be the one to win my heart.

dialogue.speaker: rama
dialogue.text: With this bow, I pledge my strength and honor to protect you, Sita.

dialogue.speaker: lakshmana
dialogue.text: Look at him lift that bow! No one can match our brother's might!

dialogue.speaker: dasharatha
dialogue.text: My son, you have proven yourself worthy of the greatest prize!
The crowd erupts in cheers as love blossoms in the air.

scenes.title: The Exile
scenes.narration: Rama was chosen to be the next king of Ayodhya. But Queen Kaikeyi, reminded of an old promise by Dasharatha, demanded that her son Bharata become king and Rama be exiled for fourteen years. Dasharatha's heart shattered, but Rama accepted the exile calmly, saying duty and truth must always be honored. Sita and Lakshmana refused to let him go alone. Together, they left the palace for the forest.

subtitles.text: Rama was chosen to be the next king of Ayodhya.
But Queen Kaikeyi, reminded of an old promise by Dasharatha, demanded that her son Bharata become king and Rama be exiled for fourteen years.
Dasharatha's heart shattered, but Rama accepted the exile calmly, saying duty and truth must always be honored.
Sita and Lakshmana refused to let him go alone.
Together, they left the palace for the forest.

dialogue.speaker: rama
dialogue.text: Duty and truth must always be honored, even in exile.

dialogue.speaker: sita
dialogue.text: I will not let you face this alone, my love.

dialogue.speaker: lakshmana
dialogue.text: Where you go, I follow. We are brothers in this journey.

dialogue.speaker: dasharatha
dialogue.text: My heart shatters at this decision, my son.

scenes.title: Life in the Forest
scenes.narration: Rama, Sita, and Lakshmana built a peaceful home in the forest at Panchavati. They lived simply among nature, learning from sages and protecting the forest dwellers. One day, a golden deer appeared — enchanting and beautiful. Sita was captivated and asked Rama to catch it. Rama followed the deer into the forest, and Lakshmana was drawn away too. It was a trap.

subtitles.text: Rama, Sita, and Lakshmana built a peaceful home in the forest at Panchavati.
They lived simply among nature, learning from sages and protecting the forest dwellers.
One day, a golden deer appeared — enchanting and beautiful.
Sita was captivated and asked Rama to catch it.
Rama followed the deer into the forest, and Lakshmana was drawn away too.
It was a trap.

dialogue.speaker: rama
dialogue.text: That golden deer... its beauty is mesmerizing. I must catch it for you, Sita.

dialogue.speaker: sita
dialogue.text: Oh Rama, look at that deer! Please, bring it to me!

dialogue.speaker: lakshmana
dialogue.text: Be cautious, brother. The forest holds many secrets.
Little did they know, it was a trap set by the cunning Ravana.

scenes.title: Ravana's Deception and Jatayu's Courage
scenes.narration: With Rama and Lakshmana away, the demon king Ravana arrived disguised as a sage and abducted Sita, carrying her away in his flying chariot. Jatayu, the noble eagle and old friend of Dasharatha, saw Sita's distress and attacked Ravana with all his might. Though old and outmatched, Jatayu fought bravely before falling. When Rama found the wounded Jatayu, the eagle told him what happened with his last breaths. Rama wept and honored Jatayu as he would his own father.

subtitles.text: With Rama and Lakshmana away, the demon king Ravana arrived disguised as a sage and abducted Sita, carrying her away in his flying chariot.
Jatayu, the noble eagle and old friend of Dasharatha, saw Sita's distress and attacked Ravana with all his might.
Though old and outmatched, Jatayu fought bravely before falling.
When Rama found the wounded Jatayu, the eagle told him what happened with his last breaths.
Rama wept and honored Jatayu as he would his own father.

dialogue.speaker: jatayu
dialogue.text: I may be old, but I won't let you take her, demon!

dialogue.speaker: ravana
dialogue.text: Foolish bird! Your courage is no match for my power!

dialogue.speaker: rama
dialogue.text: Jatayu! You fought bravely. I honor you as my father.

dialogue.speaker: sita
dialogue.text: Help me, great bird! You are my only hope!

scenes.title: The Search and the Meeting with Hanuman
scenes.narration: Grief-stricken but resolute, Rama and Lakshmana searched the forests for Sita. Their path led them to Kishkindha, where they met Sugriva, the exiled vanara king, and his minister Hanuman. Hanuman felt an instant, deep devotion to Rama. An alliance was formed: Rama would help Sugriva regain his kingdom, and Sugriva would help Rama find Sita. Hanuman pledged his life to Rama's cause.

subtitles.text: Grief-stricken but resolute, Rama and Lakshmana searched the forests for Sita.
Their path led them to Kishkindha, where they met Sugriva, the exiled vanara king, and his minister Hanuman.
Hanuman felt an instant, deep devotion to Rama.
An alliance was formed: Rama would help Sugriva regain his kingdom, and Sugriva would help Rama find Sita.
Hanuman pledged his life to Rama's cause.

dialogue.speaker: rama
dialogue.text: I will not rest until Sita is safe. We must find her, no matter the cost.

dialogue.speaker: lakshmana
dialogue.text: Brother, together we will face any challenge. I will not leave your side.

dialogue.speaker: sugriva
dialogue.text: You have my loyalty, Rama. Together, we shall reclaim what is lost.

dialogue.speaker: hanuman
dialogue.text: I pledge my life to your cause, Rama. I will be your messenger and your strength!

scenes.title: Hanuman's Leap to Lanka
scenes.narration: Hanuman stood at the edge of the southern ocean. Lanka lay beyond the vast waters. With a mighty leap powered by devotion, Hanuman soared across the sea, overcoming every obstacle. In Lanka, he searched until he found Sita in the Ashoka Vatika, surrounded by guards. He showed her Rama's ring as proof and gave her hope. Before leaving, Hanuman let himself be captured to deliver a message to Ravana, then set fire to parts of Lanka as a warning.

subtitles.text: Hanuman stood at the edge of the southern ocean.
Lanka lay beyond the vast waters.
With a mighty leap powered by devotion, Hanuman soared across the sea, overcoming every obstacle.
In Lanka, he searched until he found Sita in the Ashoka Vatika, surrounded by guards.
He showed her Rama's ring as proof and gave her hope.
Before leaving, Hanuman let himself be captured to deliver a message to Ravana, then set fire to parts of Lanka as a warning.

dialogue.speaker: hanuman
dialogue.text: With the strength of devotion, I shall leap across this ocean for my Lord!

dialogue.speaker: sita
dialogue.text: Rama's ring! Hope is not lost! My heart still beats for him!

dialogue.speaker: ravana
dialogue.text: What audacity! A mere monkey dares to challenge me?

dialogue.speaker: hanuman
dialogue.text: Let this fire be a warning, Ravana! I will not rest until Sita is free!

scenes.title: The Bridge to Lanka
scenes.narration: With the location of Sita confirmed, Rama led the vanara army to the southern shore. The vast ocean lay between them and Lanka. Under the guidance of Nala and Nila, the vanaras began building a great bridge — each stone placed with devotion, each stone floating upon the water as Rama's name was written upon them. The bridge stretched across the sea, and the army marched toward Lanka.

subtitles.text: With the location of Sita confirmed, Rama led the vanara army to the southern shore.
The vast ocean lay between them and Lanka.
Under the guidance of Nala and Nila, the vanaras began building a great bridge — each stone placed with devotion, each stone floating upon the water as Rama's name was written upon them.
The bridge stretched across the sea, and the army marched toward Lanka.

dialogue.speaker: rama
dialogue.text: Together, we shall build a bridge of hope and strength to rescue Sita!

dialogue.speaker: hanuman
dialogue.text: With each stone, we honor your name, Rama! Let the ocean witness our devotion!

dialogue.speaker: lakshmana
dialogue.text: The path to Lanka is forged by our unity. We will not falter!

dialogue.speaker: sita
dialogue.text: I believe in you, my love. Bring me home, Rama.

dialogue.speaker: ravana
dialogue.text: Foolish vanaras! You think you can challenge me with mere stones?

scenes.title: The Battle in Lanka
scenes.narration: The great battle began. Ravana's mighty army faced Rama's vanara forces. Warriors clashed on both sides. Ravana's brother Vibhishana, unable to support injustice, chose to leave Lanka and join Rama — choosing dharma over blind family loyalty. After fierce battles, Rama faced Ravana in single combat. The demon king fell, and Rama mourned even his enemy, recognizing Ravana's greatness corrupted by pride.

subtitles.text: The great battle began.
Ravana's mighty army faced Rama's vanara forces.
Warriors clashed on both sides.
Ravana's brother Vibhishana, unable to support injustice, chose to leave Lanka and join Rama — choosing dharma over blind family loyalty.
After fierce battles, Rama faced Ravana in single combat.
The demon king fell, and Rama mourned even his enemy, recognizing Ravana's greatness corrupted by pride.

dialogue.text: Even in defeat, Ravana's pride was his downfall.

scenes.title: Return to Ayodhya
scenes.narration: With Sita rescued and the battle won, Rama, Sita, Lakshmana, and Hanuman flew back to Ayodhya in the Pushpaka Vimana. Bharata, who had faithfully kept Rama's sandals on the throne for fourteen years, welcomed his brother with tears of joy. The people of Ayodhya lit thousands of lamps to celebrate Rama's return. The city shone like a constellation on earth. Rama was crowned king, and a golden era of justice began.

subtitles.text: With Sita rescued and the battle won, Rama, Sita, Lakshmana, and Hanuman flew back to Ayodhya in the Pushpaka Vimana.
Bharata, who had faithfully kept Rama's sandals on the throne for fourteen years, welcomed his brother with tears of joy.
The people of Ayodhya lit thousands of lamps to celebrate Rama's return.
The city shone like a constellation on earth.
Rama was crowned king, and a golden era of justice began.

dialogue.speaker: rama
dialogue.text: At last, I return to Ayodhya! The throne awaits, and so does justice!

dialogue.speaker: bharata
dialogue.text: Brother, your sandals have been my only crown these long years!

dialogue.speaker: sita
dialogue.text: Together, we will bring light and hope to our kingdom once more.

dialogue.speaker: lakshmana
dialogue.text: Let the celebrations begin! Ayodhya shall rejoice!

dialogue.speaker: hanuman
dialogue.text: A golden era dawns! Long live Rama, our true king!

scenes.title: What the Ramayana Teaches
scenes.narration: The Ramayana is not just a story — it is a guide for life. Rama teaches us about duty and selfless leadership. Sita teaches dignity and inner courage. Lakshmana teaches unwavering loyalty. Hanuman teaches that devotion and humility make us truly strong. Bharata teaches that power without righteousness has no value. Jatayu teaches that courage has no age. Vibhishana teaches that truth must come before blind loyalty. And Ravana reminds us that knowledge without humility can become dangerous.

subtitles.text: The Ramayana is not just a story — it is a guide for life.
Rama teaches us about duty and selfless leadership.
Sita teaches dignity and inner courage.
Lakshmana teaches unwavering loyalty.
Hanuman teaches that devotion and humility make us truly strong.
Bharata teaches that power without righteousness has no value.
Jatayu teaches that courage has no age.
Vibhishana teaches that truth must come before blind loyalty.
And Ravana reminds us that knowledge without humility can become dangerous.

dialogue.text: The Ramayana teaches us the essence of duty, courage, and righteousness.

dialogue.speaker: rama
dialogue.text: A true ruler leads with selflessness, not just power.

dialogue.speaker: sita
dialogue.text: Dignity and inner strength are the true measures of a warrior.

dialogue.speaker: lakshmana
dialogue.text: Loyalty is not just a bond; it’s a vow I will honor till my last breath!

dialogue.speaker: hanuman
dialogue.text: In devotion, we find our greatest strength!

scenes.title: The Light of Dharma
scenes.narration: The Ramayana has been told and retold for thousands of years across countless cultures and languages. Its power lies not just in its epic events, but in the timeless questions it raises: What does it mean to do the right thing? How do we stay strong when the world tests us? What is true courage, true love, true loyalty? Every generation finds its own answers inside this ancient story. The light of dharma continues to shine.

subtitles.text: The Ramayana has been told and retold for thousands of years across countless cultures and languages.
Its power lies not just in its epic events, but in the timeless questions it raises: What does it mean to do the right thing?
How do we stay strong when the world tests us?
What is true courage, true love, true loyalty?
Every generation finds its own answers inside this ancient story.
The light of dharma continues to shine.

dialogue.text: The light of dharma continues to shine through the ages.

dialogue.speaker: rama
dialogue.text: In the face of darkness, we must choose the path of righteousness.

dialogue.speaker: sita
dialogue.text: Strength lies not in power, but in unwavering faith and love.

dialogue.speaker: lakshmana
dialogue.text: Together, we will uphold dharma against all odds!

dialogue.speaker: ravana
dialogue.text: You may have won this battle, but the war for hearts endures!
